children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares rose on Tuesday, tracking Wall Street gains after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 posted their biggest advances since early August. The won strengthened 1% against the dollar, while the benchmark bond yield fell.
was up 135.91 points, or 1.94%, at 7,143.63 as of 00:59 GMT.
** The Nasdaq hit a record close on Monday, lifted by Advanced Micro Devices and other AI heavyweights, while lower oil prices and long-dated Treasury yields also boosted risk sentiment.

** The South Korean government is due to brief lawmakers on Tuesday on plans for a $350 billion US investment package, a key step as Seoul and Washington seek to finalise implementation of a trade deal that cut US tariffs on South Korean goods to 15%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution

edged 0.07% higher. ** Of the total 906 traded issues, 458 shares advanced, while 381 declined. ** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 162.8 billion won. ** The won was quoted at 1,365.7 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
